title: Quarterly orchestration blueprint: lane-coupling and release micro-sprints
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and validate a constraint-driven, lane-coupled quarterly roadmap format for the Hosted API + Model Catalog. Goal is to create a repeatable 'micro-sprint' release pattern inside the quarter that aligns model onboarding windows, capacity hedges, and canary cohorts while minimizing cross-team churn.
background: The current quarterly artifact list is long and brittle: model onboarding, endpoint releases, and capacity commits are planned in silos. We need a single orchestration blueprint that couples feature lanes (API surface and UX changes) with capacity lanes (Dedicated/Hosted pools and autoscaling hedges) and model lanes (catalog onboarding, quantization variants). This ticket scopes a blueprint, simulation of constraints, and a lightweight execution cadence to be trialed next quarter.
goals: Create lane taxonomy (feature, capacity, model, safety) and mapping to release gates
Define 2-week micro-sprint rhythm for gated model releases and endpoint updates
Produce constraint simulation (capacity, headroom, and dependency clashes) for Q2 scenarios
Ship a minimal orchestration template + runbook for PMs, Eng, and Ops
Measure delta: reduce cross-team rework by 30% during rollout windows
milestones: M1: Lane taxonomy and gate definitions — 2026-02-19
M2: Constraint simulation model and scenario deck — 2026-03-05
M3: Trial micro-sprint cadence with one model onboarding + endpoint change — 2026-03-25
M4: Runbook + templates published to Confluence and shared in PM all-hands — 2026-04-08
M5: Retro and metrics capture for Q2 trial — 2026-04-22
plan: Phase 1: Stakeholder interviews (PM, Runtime Eng, Capacity, Console, Reliability) to capture constraints and SLOs
Phase 2: Build a small simulation spreadsheet modelling request growth, dedicated pool commits, and canary capacity impact
Phase 3: Draft lane-coupling blueprint and 2-week micro-sprint checklist; circulate for review
Phase 4: Execute a single trial release pairing a model onboarding with a hosted endpoint change and dedicated capacity hedge
Phase 5: Collect signals (deploy failures, slippage, incident wakeups, cost delta) and iterate on the template
acceptance_criteria: Blueprint doc published and approved by Eng Leads and PM Director
Simulation covers at least 3 demand scenarios (baseline, +25%, spike) and shows capacity headroom thresholds
One micro-sprint trial completed without priority incidents and with documented learnings
Runbook includes explicit rollback and fallback lane mappings and is discoverable by on-call
Scorecard defined to measure cross-team rework, time-to-release, and canary failure rate
risks: Overfitting the template to Q2 specifics, reducing long-term reuse
Simulation model misses rare peak patterns and underestimates headroom needs
Insufficient stakeholder bandwidth to run micro-sprints leading to partial adoption
Model-level regressions during tight micro-sprint windows could increase rollback churn
